decision.summary: The Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 1% to 1.25%. The vote was 8-1. Dissenting: Neel Kashkari.

tone_quotes.quote: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1 to 1-1/4 percent.
On a 12-month basis, inflation has declined recently and, like the measure excluding food and energy prices, is running somewhat below 2 percent.
The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting some further strengthening in labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 12.54% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.15% and moved -6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.94% would fall by about $10.32 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4.4%, and employers added an average of 178k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.9% over the past year (May 2017); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.5%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -3 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.1%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.49% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 88%, cut 0%, hike 12%.
